reference_manual.title: STM32C0 series advanced Arm(R)-based 32-bit MCUs
reference_manual.fetch_note: st.com times out to direct curl/WebFetch from this environment (matches the survey's prior finding). Fetched successfully through the r.jina.ai text-extraction proxy. VERIFIED: 1023-page document, rev/date banner read directly off the extracted text.

extraction_caveat.finding: The proxy-extracted RM text has a systematic one-heading lag in at least two chapters (RCC 6.4.8-6.4.15, PWR 5.4.1-5.4.6): the bit-level prose paragraph immediately following a '## N.N.N Register Name' heading actually describes the PREVIOUS heading's register, not the one just printed. Root cause is almost certainly the RM's two-column PDF layout defeating linear text extraction.
extraction_caveat.how_found: RCC_IOPENR's heading (6.4.12) was immediately followed by prose describing ADCRST/TIM17RST/.../SYSCFGRST -- bits that belong to RCC_APBRSTR2 (6.4.11) per the RM's own 'Table 31: RCC register map and reset values' (6.4.24), which IS self-consistent and was used as the cross-check.
extraction_caveat.mitigation: Every field's bits/name/reset value in this drop is taken from the CMSIS-SVD (STM32C031.svd, mechanically authoritative, see svd_provenance below), not from adjacent RM prose. RM prose was used only for behavioural semantics (why a field matters) and was accepted only when it was internally self-consistent (bit names/positions in the paragraph matched the register's own field list) or corroborated by the HAL C source. Section NUMBERS cited below are reliable (the heading sequence itself is not scrambled, only the body-paragraph attachment is) -- but treat any *prose sentence* quoted from RM0490 in a 'why' as spot-checked against SVD/HAL, not as verbatim-trustworthy PDF extraction.

svd_provenance.pack: Keil.STM32C0xx_DFP v2.4.0 (2025-12-23), pdsc fetched from https://www.keil.com/pack/Keil.STM32C0xx_DFP.pdsc which points at this GitHub source repo
svd_provenance.licence: Apache-2.0. VERIFIED two ways: (1) the repo's own LICENSE file at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Open-CMSIS-Pack/STM32C0xx_DFP/main/LICENSE is the literal Apache-2.0 boilerplate; (2) the SVD file's own XML comment header states 'Copyright (c) 2024 STMicroelectronics. SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0'. No licence trap -- freely vendorable into this MIT tree with attribution, same status as cmsis_device_c0.
svd_provenance.svd_bug_found: RCC_CR's declared <resetValue> is 0x00000500 (HSIDIV[13:11]=000, i.e. /1). This contradicts BOTH RM0490 SS4.3.2 prose ('Upon power-on reset ... HCLK ... automatically set to 12 MHz') and CMSIS's own system_stm32c0xx.c, which statically initialises 'uint32_t SystemCoreClock = 12000000UL;' -- consistent only with HSIDIV=010 (/4), giving 48MHz/4=12MHz. Two independent ST sources (RM prose + CMSIS startup code) agree with each other and disagree with the SVD's stated register reset value. Treat the SVD's resetValue for RCC_CR as WRONG for the HSIDIV field; this repo's regmap below uses the RM/CMSIS-confirmed value (HSIDIV=010) and flags it in rcc.json.

hal_provenance.note: STM32CubeC0's top-level repo (STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeC0) vendors this as a git submodule; both the top-level repo name and this submodule's name were renamed with hyphens at some point after the .gitmodules entry was written (STM32CubeC0/.gitmodules still says 'stm32c0xx_hal_driver.git' with underscores; GitHub 301-redirects that to 'stm32c0xx-hal-driver'). field_kind_taxonomy_as_applied_here.note: The 8-kind taxonomy (rw / ready-follows / mirrors / clears-instantly / self-clearing / w1c+rc_w0 / counter / hw-coded) was designed by a sibling agent (stm-soc) earlier this session. I could not locate its schema/definition artifact on disk (checked webui/parts/schemas, tools/, docs/, and the shared scratchpad) and messaged stm-soc directly to ask for it; no reply had arrived by the time this drop was written. The definitions below are MY reconstruction from the 8 kind-names plus the read-purity rule stated in my brief, cross-checked against the concrete polarity table already in docs/architectures.md SS3.4 (which distinguishes 'status mirrors enable' from 'register stores and reflects' -- exactly the ready-follows/mirrors split used here). Flag this as UNVERIFIED against the original design; reconcile if/when stm-soc's actual schema surfaces.
field_kind_taxonomy_as_applied_here.rw: Plain read-write storage. Read returns the last value written (masked to defined bits); write stores unconditionally. No cross-field or time dependency.
field_kind_taxonomy_as_applied_here.ready-follows: A read-only status bit that tracks a paired enable bit: reads 1 once the enable has been set, reads 0 once the enable has been cleared. Models the real hardware's settle time as instantaneous, which is exactly the Renode 'ready-mirrors-enable' pattern architectures.md SS3.4 recommends for unsticking HAL_GetTick-gated spins.
field_kind_taxonomy_as_applied_here.mirrors: A read-only (or read-mostly) field whose value is defined as a pure copy of a DIFFERENT field's most recently written value, with no separate enable/disable latch semantics of its own -- e.g. RCC_CFGR.SWS mirroring RCC_CFGR.SW once a clock switch is requested.
field_kind_taxonomy_as_applied_here.clears-instantly: A status bit that is 1 exactly while some external condition holds and reverts to 0 the instant that condition stops holding, with no software action needed to clear it. Not used in this drop's minimum register set (candidate for USART_ISR.TXE/RXNE if this simulator ever models buffer occupancy as instantaneous rather than time-delayed).
field_kind_taxonomy_as_applied_here.self-clearing: A bit software SETS to request a one-shot hardware action; hardware autonomously clears it back to 0 once that action completes, with no discrete w1c write required. Example in the wider FLASH register set (out of this drop's scope): FLASH_CR.OBL_LAUNCH, whose own SVD description literally says 'automatically cleared upon completion'.
field_kind_taxonomy_as_applied_here.w1c+rc_w0: A hardware-set error/event flag that stays 1 until software explicitly clears it, either by writing 1 to the same bit position (w1c) or via a companion write-1-to-clear register (e.g. USART_ICR clearing USART_ISR flags, RCC_CICR clearing RCC_CIFR flags). Not used in this drop's minimum register set; RCC_CSR2's reset-cause flags are the nearest in-scope example and are modelled as a distinct pattern (RMVF-gated) below rather than force-fit into this bucket.
field_kind_taxonomy_as_applied_here.counter: A field that advances autonomously with virtual time/cycles rather than purely in response to a write. Not present in this drop -- SysTick is the only counter in the minimum boot set and is explicitly out of the regmap system (in-core Armv6-M SCS, not a vendor peripheral) per my brief.
field_kind_taxonomy_as_applied_here.hw-coded: A register where no ('bits','name','kind') tuple is a sufficient description, because the read-purity rule in .claude/rules (a register is data iff every read is a pure function of stored state + virtual time AND every write only stores) is violated. Enumerated explicitly in stm32c031c6_hw_coded_registers.md-equivalent section of the findings report; see regmap files' "hw_coded" blocks.
